title: Quiet Customers
story: Which customers have never ordered anything? An inner join would hide them, so use a LEFT JOIN.
goal: Show the names of customers who have no orders.
starter:
SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer, filling order columns with NULL when nothing matches.
After the join, keep the rows where the order id IS NULL.
SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;
socratic: What does a LEFT JOIN do with customers who have no match?
How do you spot them afterwards?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;
alt: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders);
